title: Messenger Pigeons (fork, pipe, exec)
hints: run_child: pid = fork(); in the child (pid == 0): _exit(child_main()); in the parent: waitpid(pid, &status, 0), then WIFEXITED(status) ? WEXITSTATUS(status) : 128 + WTERMSIG(status).
The child must end with _exit(), never `return` and never exit(): returning would let a second copy of the test program carry on running the tests.
capture: fflush(stdout) BEFORE fork (or buffered text is duplicated into the child). int fd[2]; pipe(fd). Child: dup2(fd[1], STDOUT_FILENO); close both fd; run; fflush(stdout); _exit(0).

capture, parent side: close(fd[1]) FIRST - while any write end is open, read() never reports end-of-file. Then loop read(fd[0], buf, sizeof buf) until it returns 0, close(fd[0]), and only then waitpid.
Read before you wait: a pipe holds about 64 KiB. A child writing more blocks until the parent reads; a parent stuck in waitpid never reads. That is a deadlock between two processes.

run_program: build std::vector<char*> from argv (const_cast<char*>(s.c_str())) plus a final nullptr; in the child, after dup2: execvp(args[0], args.data()); _exit(127);  - the line after execvp only runs if exec failed.
